gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the 600 W in BLUETTI's Apex 300 + 3× 200 W kit cannot be wired as one series string (3 × 24.6 V Voc = 73.8 V against a 12–60 V solar input), while the ALLPOWERS 600 W kits use one 44 V folding panel on one MC4-to-XT60 cable into inputs rated 1,000 W (R2500 V2) and 2,000 W (R3500).
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts (cited), OutageReady, and Dealectric's own under-$3,000 (cited), panels-included and under-$1,000 pages. StormWatts already gives the SP200L's Voc 24.6 V and Isc 10.8 A and does the series/parallel arithmetic for two panels on the Elite 200 V2, and it flags a kit whose panel exceeds the station's cap (Explorer 2000 v2 + 500 W). OutageReady states the general rule that series adds voltage and the input range must not be exceeded. Dealectric's under-$1,000 page already says the P1800 is rated 650 W so its 600 W panel is not clipped, and the under-$3,000 page says the R3500 takes up to 2,000 W. What none of them has is the three-panel case for a 600 W BLUETTI kit, and none gives Voc, Isc or wiring for the EcoFlow DELTA 3800 Gen4's 4 × 160 W panels. So rivals hold the method and most of the numbers; only the 600 W-specific application is new. I could not open ALLPOWERS's full spec tables today (HTTP 429), so the ALLPOWERS side rests on listing text only.
decides: It confirms rather than changes the pick. The ALLPOWERS kits that ship now deliver their 600 W as a single SP039 panel with the cable in the box, so there is no wiring decision: the R3500 + SP039 ($1,753.93 link price, $1,993.10 store) runs at 30% of its 2,000 W solar rating. The BLUETTI Apex 300 + 3× 200 W ($2,279.05 link price, $2,399.00 store, pre-order to late January 2027) needs its three panels split across the station's two solar inputs, because three in series exceed 60 V on BLUETTI's own range. That is a second reason, after the dispatch date, to name it as the wait-for option and not the pick. The R2500 V2 + SP039 (pre-order, Dec 11, 2026) fits its 1,000 W input with room to spare.

findings.label: Three 200 W panels in one series string against the 12–60 V input
findings.value: 73.8 V Voc, 13.8 V over the 60 V ceiling
findings.source_title: Connecting solar panels to solar generator (BLUETTI blog)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 3 × 24.6 V (StormWatts' SP200L Voc) = 73.8 V against BLUETTI's 12–60 V range. Two in series = 49.2 V, which fits; StormWatts puts two in series at about 56.5 V on a −4°F morning using its own assumed −0.33%/°C coefficient. Three in parallel = 3 × 10.8 A = 32.4 A Isc, under the 40 A total. A layout inside the published numbers is two in series on one input and the third on the other. This assumes the kit's panels are SP200L, which the listing does not state.
